messages.subject: Error from secrBVN and region.N
parts:
Hi all,

I made a multi-session capthist with multiple trap files (unique trap layouts). Then I fitted several full likelihood models with anisotropic.fit, e.g., D~session + slope g0~bk

But when I used region.N to get abundance, I got an error saying:

> region.N(secr19)
Error in coords %*% rm : non-conformable arguments.

Here is my RData (Don't know if it's the proper way to send data here):

https://drive.google.com/file/d/11YkkS4zCHZPazjYlQppNv-QLb_q1YpXA/view?usp=sharing

In my case, seems like all models (secr13, secr15, ..., secr19) fitted by anisotropic.fit returned this error.

I'd like to know if region.N doesn't apply to secrBVN or I did something wrong.

Many thanks!!

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Error from secrBVN and region.N
parts:
Well, secrBVN is a rather specialised package meant to support the paper in Ecology (2019), and only available on GitHub, so I'm not promising it will be kept compatible with current secr, but...

The reason region.N() didn't work for you turns out to be two obscure bugs, one concerning multi-session data with varying detectors and one concerning user-specified distance functions (secrBVN uses a custom distance function based on geoR). These both needed to be fixed irrespective of secrBVN, so thanks for reporting the issue with examples that made it easy to trace the problem.

I think I have fixed the issues in a pre-release version. This is available as source code at www.otago.ac.nz/density/zip/secr_4.5.9.tar.gz and as windows binary at www.otago.ac.nz/density/zip/secr_4.5.9.zip (expect further changes in the pre-release version before it is submtted to CRAN).

The problem arose only with se.N = TRUE. I now get, e.g.
> region.N(secr19)
